speeches.speaker: Josh Frydenberg
speeches.brief: Moved the second reading of the Statute Law Revision Bill (No. 2) 2014, which corrects drafting errors, replaces the word servant with employee, removes gender-specific language, and consolidates more than 25 definitions sections in the Veterans' Entitlements Act 1986, for a compliance cost saving of $420,000.

speeches.speaker: Josh Frydenberg
speeches.brief: Moved to suspend standing orders so debate, amendments and votes on the Omnibus Repeal Day (Spring 2014) Bill 2014, the Amending Acts 1970 to 1979 Repeal Bill 2014 and the Statute Law Revision Bill (No. 2) 2014 could be managed together, saying deregulation and cutting red tape were a priority for the government.

speeches.speaker: Shayne Neumann
speeches.brief: Criticised the three repeal bills for delivering only $1.855 million in total savings, the largest single item being $1.16 million from aged care notification changes, contrasted this with Labor's Seamless National Economy reforms estimated to save $4 billion a year, and raised concerns that changes to the Stronger Futures in the Northern Territory Act would remove a requirement for independent review of alcohol management laws.

speeches.speaker: Lisa Chesters
speeches.brief: Argued that the Omnibus Repeal Day bill and related statute law revision bills are being used to sneak through the resumption of fuel excise indexation without proper debate, noting the increase and the start of prepolling for the Victorian state election will both occur in 12 days.

speeches.speaker: Mark Dreyfus
speeches.brief: Argued that the government's Statute Law Revision Bill and Amending Act Repeal Bill are routine housekeeping dressed up as deregulation, noting the repeal bill would remove around 650 spent amending acts from the 1970s that the explanatory memorandum itself admits will not change the substance of any law.

speeches.speaker: Josh Frydenberg
speeches.brief: Argued that the government's repeal day bills would deliver $2.1 billion in compliance savings and abolish bodies including the Fishing Industry Policy Council, and criticised Labor for introducing 21000 additional regulations while doing nothing to streamline schemes such as Comcare or the Do Not Call Register.
